definition_text: Article 325: Public Incitement to Violence and Hatred. Article 325 (1) Whoever in print, through radio, television, computer system or network, at a public gathering or in some other way publicly incites to or makes available to the public tracts, pictures or other material instigating violence or hatred directed against a group of persons or a member of such a group on account of their race, religion, national or ethnic origin, descent, colour, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or any other characteristics shall be punished by imprisonment not exceeding three years. (2) The same punishment as referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article shall be inflicted on whoever publicly approves of, denies or grossly trivializes the crimes of genocide, crimes of aggression, crimes against humanity or war crimes, directed against a group of persons or a member of such a group on account of their race, religion, national or ethnic origin, descent or colour in a manner likely to incite to violence or hatred against such a group or a member of such a group. (3) The attempt to carry out or commit criminal offences referred to in paragraph 1 and 2 of this Article shall be punishable
